question.text: A pair of diamonds are released from rest at an identical elevation, one falling 1.0 s after the other. Find the time elapsed since the release of the initial diamond at which the vertical gap separating the two stones reaches 10 m. (Use g = 10 m/s²)
conditions: released from the same initial height

solution.approach: Write the distance fallen by each diamond as a function of time from the first diamond's release, then set the gap between them to 10 m to find that time.

steps.text: Measure time t from when the first diamond is released. Its distance fallen is ½gt².
The second diamond is released 1.0 s later, so for t ≥ 1 s its distance fallen is ½g(t − 1)².
The gap between them, for t ≥ 1 s, is the difference of these two distances.
Set the gap to 10 m and solve for t.

common_mistakes.text: Ignoring that the second diamond is already falling and solving 5t² = 10 for the gap gives t = √2 ≈ 1.41 s; the distance fallen since t = 1.0 s must be subtracted.
